summary: Interface conventions: name the object option name (or alias it), accept all common boolean spellings via type='bool', and avoid imperative action/command options.
questions: What should I call the option that identifies the object my module manages?
How do I make my module accept yes/no/true/false for booleans?

answer_card.title: Designing module interfaces
answer_card.answer_md:
- Call the object option `name`, or accept `name` as an alias.
- Use `type='bool'` so `yes`, `no`, `true`, `false`, etc. all work.
- Avoid `action`/`command` options; they're imperative, not declarative.
